# AI policy — Christian Luciani

<!-- Generated by pasco export ai-policy (ai-policy v1, as of 2026-10-27) — regenerate rather than edit. -->

**Policy version:** 1 · **Effective date:** 2026-10-27

## The stance (SPEC §12 M9, quoted verbatim)

> **private-first default**: `robots.txt` on published surfaces **blocks** AI-training crawlers (CCBot / vendor AI crawlers) and user data ships **without** an open license; entering corpora or open-licensing data requires the profile owner's explicit opt-in (consent field — schema work deferred with Q10).

In plain terms: the crawlers named below under **Allowed** — search and
answer indexing, and a fetch a user asked for — may read this site; the
crawlers named under **Blocked** may not. This is an explicit list, not a
wildcard default: a crawler that is **not** named here is **not restricted by
this file**. That boundary is deliberate — the owner states a policy over the
crawlers whose classification they have checked against the operator's own
documentation, and makes no claim about the rest of the web.

## Who can change this

The profile owner. The list below is generated from the ai-policy registry that
ships with `pasco` — never typed into this file — and every entry carries the
operator's own documentation URL and the date it was read. Regenerate with
`pasco export ai-policy --out <dir>`; `pasco export ai-policy --check` fails
when an entry is unsourced or older than 180 days, so this file cannot rot
silently.

## Date

As of 2026-10-27. The stamp is the registry's review date, not a generation
timestamp: two runs on different days produce byte-identical files.
